claims.text: Module 6 is a 10-minute concepts lesson requiring decentralized API, Core and Platform access, and endpoint selection, completed by the dapi quiz.
DAPI uses Dash's masternode infrastructure to expose layer 1 Core and layer 2 Platform functionality through an API.
Clients can use different DAPI instances according to network resource availability rather than depend on one mandatory provider instance.
JSON-RPC exposes limited Core information, while gRPC covers Platform, richer Core operations, and event streams.
Core-facing operations include block and chain queries, transaction broadcast and lookup, and subscriptions to Core updates.
Platform-facing operations include identity, contract, and document queries plus state-transition broadcast and confirmation; supported queries can return proofs.
A higher-level SDK is the normal application path because it handles connection management and data serialization; direct DAPI access can be useful for debugging.
Pinned SDK 4.1.1 begins node selection with a network preset or explicit HTTPS addresses; a trusted context can supply discovered addresses, but explicit addresses remain authoritative.
Pinned transport settings support retries and failed-address exclusion, and the underlying DAPI client provides retries and load balancing.
For this lesson, endpoint selection comprises choosing the Core or Platform API surface and choosing among DAPI node providers.
TLS, decentralized provider selection, and Platform proof verification address transport security, availability, and response integrity respectively.

conflicts.description: The vendored 3.1.0 connection tutorial says custom remote-devnet addresses are unsupported, while pinned SDK 4.1.1 documentation and types support devnet address lists.
conflicts.resolution: Remote-devnet configuration is outside this concepts lesson and is omitted. Pinned 4.1.1 package types remain authoritative for SDK shape.
